steps.message:
Before I touch it — this one's a published contract, not just a string.

`routes/users.js:6` is the only occurrence:

```js
users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),
```

The README is explicit about what depends on it:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

Renaming in place breaks all three the moment it deploys — and shipped iOS builds can't be fixed forward. The consistency goal is real (`/orders` already returns `order_id`/`user_id`), but the README says this class of change goes through a version bump.

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId in the same response. New consumers get the snake_case name immediately, existing clients keep working, and userId is dropped once the iOS and partner-export consumers have migrated. No version bump needed.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: What the README prescribes: leave GET /users as-is and add a v2 route that returns user_id. Cleanest contract story, but needs a routing decision and more scaffolding than exists in this repo today.

options.label: Rename in place
options.description: Exactly what was asked: change userId to user_id and nothing else. Breaking change for the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export. Choose this if those consumers are already handled or the endpoint is not actually live yet.
